thread:
Maya R: Hey team — thinking about adding a "sigil" field to runtime configs as an atomic activation key for multi-stage rollouts. Idea: attach a short opaque token to a config snapshot so we can safely promote/rollback without relying on patch diffs.
Sam K: Curious, name aside — what's the problem this solves vs snapshot ids + commit metadata?
Maya R: Two things: 1) console UX: operators can copy/paste a sigil into a quick-promote input instead of navigating snapshots. 2) runtime: route-by-sigil in router to tie traffic slices to exact activation atomicity (avoid partial apply if some services lag).
Liam: route-by-sigil sounds like adding another selector dimension. How would that interact with cohort hashing and quotas?
Maya R: Good Q. Proposal: sigil only affects config activation semantics, not cohort hashing. Router evaluates config version via (scope, sigil) -> resolved policy. Quotas are still keyed to route id + model, so no quota duplication unless a sigil explicitly introduces routing variants.
Anna: Can we do a dry-run preview first? UI should show diff + telemetry baseline for last N minutes. Ops will want a simulated traffic map.
Sam K: We have a preview API already. Can we reuse /preview/config? It returns effective route map for a given snapshot. Needs extension to accept sigil and simulate activation windows.
Maya R: Yep extend preview API to accept sigil param and a lookback window. Also add a telemetry gate requirement: previews must run through shadow-proxy to collect sample responses for quality baselining.
ops-bot: deploy-check: preview-api v2 deployed to staging at 2024-11-03T14:08:12Z :white_check_mark:
Liam: Concern: increasing cardinality of runtime keys. If teams create lots of sigils, we could blow up cache entries and monitoring. Do we have TTL / garbage policy?
Maya R: Propose sigils be ephemeral by default: auto-expire after 7 days unless pinned. Console pinning requires two-person approval for enterprise accounts.
Anna: Two-person pin + audit log sounds good. Also need a console affordance to show which sigils are currently active in production and the associated telemetry summary (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta).
Sam K: From API shape perspective, we should keep sigil as a string field on Snapshot metadata: { "sigil": "s-lj3k", "author": ..., "expires_at": ... }. Then router gets a resolved snapshot id when activation happens.
Liam: Does activation change how we roll out? Example: canary by sigil -> partial traffic attached to sigil only? If so need to ensure quota enforcement is consistent when both old and new sigil traffic co-exist.
Maya R: Yes canary by sigil should be supported. Quota enforcement will map traffic to the effective route id (route id is stable), but usage attribution must carry sigil tag so we can roll metrics and quota buckets per sigil for the rollout window.
Anna: That implies billing tags and console cost breakdowns need to accept a sigil dimension. Noted.
Sam K: One risk: accidental drift where config keys diverge but sigil is same. We need an invariant: sigil maps to an immutable snapshot hash. If someone changes snapshot content, new sigil must be required.
Maya R: Agreed. Enforce at API: creating/updating snapshot with same sigil returns 409 unless force=true and includes explicit reason + audit annotation.
Liam: Can we add a lint rule in the console to warn if a pinned sigil hasn't received telemetry for > 4 hours? Avoid promoting stale configs.
Anna: Telemetry gate should be more formal: require N samples and a regression-check against baseline thresholds (latency + quality) before allowing full promotion. Expose as opt-out.
Sam K: Implementation detail: router currently resolves config id via etcd index + version. Adding sigil lookup requires a small service that maps sigil->snapshot-hash. We can keep cache TTL low and invalidate on pin/unpin.
Maya R: Thinking of a soft-fallback: if sigil lookup fails at runtime, route should fallback to default snapshot for that scope and emit a metric sigil.resolve.miss with tags. No hard failure.
ops-bot: new metric: sigil.resolve.miss created in prod -> metric-team notified :bell:
Liam: Stacking these pieces, we also need a runbook: how to rollback a sigil-promoted config if production shows regressions. Steps: 1) promote a previous sigil (via console quick-promote) 2) if rollback fails, circuit to route to backup model variant 3) alert on-call and open incident.
Anna: Add a guard: quick-promote button requires either a dry-run + 2 reviewers OR a canary window threshold like <1% error delta. Console should show the gating status.
Sam K: Backend API pseudo:
```
POST /snapshots/{id}/activate
{ "sigil": "s-abc", "mode": "canary", "canary_pct": 5, "pin": false }
```
Server returns activation object with rollout_id. Activation rejected if sigil already exists unless force.
Maya R: UX note: make the sigil human-copyable, short but not guessable. Use base36 6 chars.
Liam: Telemetry storage cost could rise if we retain per-sigil time-series. Strategy: aggregate short-term (7d) per-sigil metrics then roll to aggregated baseline long-term.
Anna: We should also ensure the console timeline UI can group sigils by snapshot and show overlapping rollouts.
Sam K: Final ask from infra: we need a migration plan. Start with preview-only mode (sigil accepted by preview API, no runtime resolution). Phase 2: router reads sigil map in dry-run mode (no traffic split). Phase 3: full canary + pinning.
Maya R: Timeline proposal: preview-only in 2 weeks, dry-run router in 6 weeks, full rollout in 10 weeks. I'll create an RFC and a console mock.
Liam: Add me as reviewer on RFC. Also add a perf budget so we can rollback if cache miss rate > 0.1%.
Anna: I'll draft telemetry gating thresholds and a sample eval prompt set for quality checks.
Sam K: I'll open a small API ticket and include contract examples + 409 semantics.
Maya R: Thanks all. tagging @ops-bot to create RFC issue and link mockups.
ops-bot: RFC issue created: https://go/infra/issue/4592 (Maya R assigned) :spiral_note_pad:
Sam K: One last thought — name "sigil" is fun but maybe call it "activation-token" to be explicit in logs (searchable). Up to you.
Maya R: Open to rename — will pick a human-friendly short name in RFC. For now we used "sigil" in mocks.
Anna: :thumbsup: 
Liam: :+1: 
Maya R: ok wrapping up — I'll post the RFC link here when ready and schedule a 30m sync next Tue.
